audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Exodus / Shemot covenant ordinances text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Hebrew servant laws, female servant protections, violence penalties, lex talionis, injury liability, and property/animal laws. Strong human-dignity safeguards required.

verses.restored: And these are the judgments/ordinances that you shall place before them.

familiar.text: Now these are the judgments which thou shalt set before them.

modern.text: “These are the ordinances that you are to set before them:

original.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּשִׂ֖ים לִפְנֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: When you buy a Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve, and in seventh he shall go out free, without payment.

familiar.text: If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.

modern.text: If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years. But in the seventh year, he shall go free without paying anything.

original.text: כִּ֤י תִקְנֶה֙ עֶ֣בֶד עִבְרִ֔י שֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים יַעֲבֹ֑ד וּבַ֨שְּׁבִעִ֔ת יֵצֵ֥א לַֽחָפְשִׁ֖י חִנָּֽם

verses.restored: If he comes in by himself, he shall go out by himself; if husband of a woman, his woman/wife shall go out with him.

familiar.text: If he came in by himself, he shall go out by himself: if he were married, then his wife shall go out with him.

modern.text: If he arrived alone, he is to leave alone; if he arrived with a wife, she is to leave with him.

original.text: אִם בְּגַפּ֥וֹ יָבֹ֖א בְּגַפּ֣וֹ יֵצֵ֑א אִם בַּ֤עַל אִשָּׁה֙ ה֔וּא וְיָצְאָ֥ה אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ עִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: If his master gives him a woman/wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to her master, and he shall go out by himself.

familiar.text: If his master have given him a wife, and she have born him sons or daughters; the wife and her children shall be her master’s, and he shall go out by himself.

modern.text: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to her master, and only the man shall go free.

original.text: אִם אֲדֹנָיו֙ יִתֶּן ל֣וֹ אִשָּׁ֔ה וְיָלְדָה ל֥וֹ בָנִ֖ים א֣וֹ בָנ֑וֹת הָאִשָּׁ֣ה וִילָדֶ֗יהָ תִּהְיֶה֙ לַֽאדֹנֶ֔יהָ וְה֖וּא יֵצֵ֥א בְגַפּֽוֹ

verses.restored: But if the servant clearly says, I love my master, my woman/wife, and my children; I will not go out free,

familiar.text: And if the servant shall plainly say, I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free:

modern.text: But if the servant declares, ‘I love my master and my wife and children; I do not want to go free,’

original.text: וְאִם אָמֹ֤ר יֹאמַר֙ הָעֶ֔בֶד אָהַ֨בְתִּי֙ אֶת אֲדֹנִ֔י אֶת אִשְׁתִּ֖י וְאֶת בָּנָ֑י לֹ֥א אֵצֵ֖א חָפְשִֽׁי

verses.restored: then his master shall bring him to the Divine; he shall bring him to door or doorpost, and his master shall pierce his ear with awl, and he shall serve him into the age.

familiar.text: Then his master shall bring him unto the judges; he shall also bring him to the door, or unto the door post; and his master shall bore his ear through with an aul; and he shall serve him for ever.

modern.text: then his master is to bring him before the judges. And he shall take him to the door or doorpost and pierce his ear with an awl. Then he shall serve his master for life.

original.text: וְהִגִּישׁ֤וֹ אֲדֹנָיו֙ אֶל הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְהִגִּישׁוֹ֙ אֶל הַדֶּ֔לֶת א֖וֹ אֶל הַמְּזוּזָ֑ה וְרָצַ֨ע אֲדֹנָ֤יו אֶת אָזְנוֹ֙ בַּמַּרְצֵ֔עַ וַעֲבָד֖וֹ לְעֹלָֽם

verses.restored: When a man sells his daughter as female servant, she shall not go out as male servants go out.

familiar.text: And if a man sell his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out as the menservants do.

modern.text: And if a man sells his daughter as a servant, she is not to go free as the menservants do.

original.text: וְכִֽי יִמְכֹּ֥ר אִ֛ישׁ אֶת בִּתּ֖וֹ לְאָמָ֑ה לֹ֥א תֵצֵ֖א כְּצֵ֥את הָעֲבָדִֽים

verses.restored: If she is harmful/displeasing in eyes of her master who designated her for himself, then he shall let her be redeemed; he has no authority to sell her to foreign people, because he has dealt treacherously with her.

familiar.text: If she please not her master, who hath betrothed her to himself, then shall he let her be redeemed: to sell her unto a strange nation he shall have no power, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her.

modern.text: If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master who had designated her for himself, he must allow her to be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to foreigners, since he has broken faith with her.

original.text: אִם רָעָ֞ה בְּעֵינֵ֧י אֲדֹנֶ֛יהָ אֲשֶׁר לא יְעָדָ֖הּ וְהֶפְדָּ֑הּ לְעַ֥ם נָכְרִ֛י לֹא יִמְשֹׁ֥ל לְמָכְרָ֖הּ בְּבִגְדוֹ בָֽהּ

verses.restored: If he designates her for his son, he shall do to her according to judgment/right of daughters.

familiar.text: And if he have betrothed her unto his son, he shall deal with her after the manner of daughters.

modern.text: And if he chooses her for his son, he must deal with her as with a daughter.

original.text: וְאִם לִבְנ֖וֹ יִֽיעָדֶ֑נָּה כְּמִשְׁפַּ֥ט הַבָּנ֖וֹת יַעֲשֶׂה לָּֽהּ

verses.restored: If he takes another for himself, her food, clothing, and marital rights he shall not diminish.

familiar.text: If he take him another wife; her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish.

modern.text: If he takes another wife, he must not reduce the food, clothing, or marital rights of his first wife.

original.text: אִם אַחֶ֖רֶת יִֽקַּֽח ל֑וֹ שְׁאֵרָ֛הּ כְּסוּתָ֥הּ וְעֹנָתָ֖הּ לֹ֥א יִגְרָֽע

verses.restored: If he does not do these three for her, then she shall go out for nothing, without silver.

familiar.text: And if he do not these three unto her, then shall she go out free without money.

modern.text: If, however, he does not provide her with these three things, she is free to go without monetary payment. Personal Injury Laws

original.text: וְאִם שְׁלָ֨שׁ אֵ֔לֶּה לֹ֥א יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה לָ֑הּ וְיָצְאָ֥ה חִנָּ֖ם אֵ֥ין כָּֽסֶף

verses.restored: One striking a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death.

familiar.text: He that smiteth a man, so that he die, shall be surely put to death.

modern.text: Whoever strikes and kills a man must surely be put to death.

original.text: מַכֵּ֥ה אִ֛ישׁ וָמֵ֖ת מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת

verses.restored: But one who did not lie in wait, but Divine let it happen to his hand, I will appoint for you a place where he may flee.

familiar.text: And if a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand; then I will appoint thee a place whither he shall flee.

modern.text: If, however, he did not lie in wait, but God allowed it to happen, then I will appoint for you a place where he may flee.

original.text: וַאֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א צָדָ֔ה וְהָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אִנָּ֣ה לְיָד֑וֹ וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י לְךָ֙ מָק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָנ֖וּס שָֽׁמָּה

verses.restored: But when a man acts arrogantly against his companion to kill him with cunning, from my altar you shall take him to die.

familiar.text: But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour, to slay him with guile; thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.

modern.text: But if a man schemes and acts willfully against his neighbor to kill him, you must take him away from My altar to be put to death.

original.text: וְכִֽי יָזִ֥ד אִ֛ישׁ עַל רֵעֵ֖הוּ לְהָרְג֣וֹ בְעָרְמָ֑ה מֵעִ֣ם מִזְבְּחִ֔י תִּקָּחֶ֖נּוּ לָמֽוּת

verses.restored: One striking father or mother shall surely be put to death.

familiar.text: And he that smiteth his father, or his mother, shall be surely put to death.

modern.text: Whoever strikes his father or mother must surely be put to death.

original.text: וּמַכֵּ֥ה אָבִ֛יו וְאִמּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת

verses.restored: One stealing a human and selling him, or he is found in his hand, shall surely be put to death.

familiar.text: And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, or if he be found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.

modern.text: Whoever kidnaps another man must be put to death, whether he sells him or the man is found in his possession.

original.text: וְגֹנֵ֨ב אִ֧ישׁ וּמְכָר֛וֹ וְנִמְצָ֥א בְיָד֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת

verses.restored: One cursing father or mother shall surely be put to death.

familiar.text: And he that curseth his father, or his mother, shall surely be put to death.

modern.text: Anyone who curses his father or mother must surely be put to death.

original.text: וּמְקַלֵּ֥ל אָבִ֛יו וְאִמּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת

verses.restored: When men quarrel and one strikes his companion with stone or fist, and he does not die but falls to bed,

familiar.text: And if men strive together, and one smite another with a stone, or with his fist, and he die not, but keepeth his bed:

modern.text: If men are quarreling and one strikes the other with a stone or a fist, and he does not die but is confined to bed,

original.text: וְכִֽי יְרִיבֻ֣ן אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְהִכָּה אִישׁ֙ אֶת רֵעֵ֔הוּ בְּאֶ֖בֶן א֣וֹ בְאֶגְרֹ֑ף וְלֹ֥א יָמ֖וּת וְנָפַ֥ל לְמִשְׁכָּֽב

verses.restored: if he rises and walks outside on his staff, the striker shall be cleared; only his sitting/time lost he shall pay, and healing he shall surely heal.

familiar.text: If he rise again, and walk abroad upon his staff, then shall he that smote him be quit: only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall cause him to be thoroughly healed.

modern.text: then the one who struck him shall go unpunished, as long as the other can get up and walk around outside with his staff. Nevertheless, he must compensate the man for his lost work and see that he is completely healed.

original.text: אִם יָק֞וּם וְהִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּח֛וּץ עַל מִשְׁעַנְתּ֖וֹ וְנִקָּ֣ה הַמַּכֶּ֑ה רַ֥ק שִׁבְתּ֛וֹ יִתֵּ֖ן וְרַפֹּ֥א יְרַפֵּֽא

verses.restored: When a man strikes his male servant or female servant with rod, and the servant dies under his hand, avenging he shall be avenged.

familiar.text: And if a man smite his servant, or his maid, with a rod, and he die under his hand; he shall be surely punished.

modern.text: If a man strikes his manservant or maidservant with a rod, and the servant dies by his hand, he shall surely be punished.

original.text: וְכִֽי יַכֶּה֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶת עַבְדּ֜וֹ א֤וֹ אֶת אֲמָתוֹ֙ בַּשֵּׁ֔בֶט וּמֵ֖ת תַּ֣חַת יָד֑וֹ נָקֹ֖ם יִנָּקֵֽם

verses.restored: Yet if the servant stands a day or two, he shall not be avenged, for he is his silver.

familiar.text: Notwithstanding, if he continue a day or two, he shall not be punished: for he is his money.

modern.text: However, if the servant gets up after a day or two, the owner shall not be punished, since the servant is his property.

original.text: אַ֥ךְ אִם י֛וֹם א֥וֹ יוֹמַ֖יִם יַעֲמֹ֑ד לֹ֣א יֻקַּ֔ם כִּ֥י כַסְפּ֖וֹ הֽוּא

verses.restored: When men fight and strike a pregnant woman and her children go out, but no harm follows, he shall surely be fined as the woman's husband lays upon him, and he shall give by judges.

familiar.text: If men strive, and hurt a woman with child, so that her fruit depart from her, and yet no mischief follow: he shall be surely punished, according as the woman’s husband will lay upon him; and he shall pay as the judges determine.

modern.text: If men who are fighting strike a pregnant woman and her child is born prematurely, but there is no further injury, he shall surely be fined as the woman’s husband demands and as the court allows.

original.text: וְכִֽי יִנָּצ֣וּ אֲנָשִׁ֗ים וְנָ֨גְפ֜וּ אִשָּׁ֤ה הָרָה֙ וְיָצְא֣וּ יְלָדֶ֔יהָ וְלֹ֥א יִהְיֶ֖ה אָס֑וֹן עָנ֣וֹשׁ יֵעָנֵ֗שׁ כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָשִׁ֤ית עָלָיו֙ בַּ֣עַל הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וְנָתַ֖ן בִּפְלִלִֽים

verses.restored: But if harm follows, then you shall give life for life,

familiar.text: And if any mischief follow, then thou shalt give life for life,

modern.text: But if a serious injury results, then you must require a life for a life—

original.text: וְאִם אָס֖וֹן יִהְיֶ֑ה וְנָתַתָּ֥ה נֶ֖פֶשׁ תַּ֥חַת נָֽפֶשׁ

verses.restored: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,

familiar.text: Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,

modern.text: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,

original.text: עַ֚יִן תַּ֣חַת עַ֔יִן שֵׁ֖ן תַּ֣חַת שֵׁ֑ן יָ֚ד תַּ֣חַת יָ֔ד רֶ֖גֶל תַּ֥חַת רָֽגֶל

verses.restored: burn for burn, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.

familiar.text: Burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.

modern.text: burn for burn, wound for wound, and stripe for stripe.

original.text: כְּוִיָּה֙ תַּ֣חַת כְּוִיָּ֔ה פֶּ֖צַע תַּ֣חַת פָּ֑צַע חַבּוּרָ֕ה תַּ֖חַת חַבּוּרָֽה

verses.restored: When a man strikes eye of his male servant or eye of his female servant and destroys it, he shall send the servant away free for the eye.

familiar.text: And if a man smite the eye of his servant, or the eye of his maid, that it perish; he shall let him go free for his eye’s sake.

modern.text: If a man strikes and blinds the eye of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the eye.

original.text: וְכִֽי יַכֶּ֨ה אִ֜ישׁ אֶת עֵ֥ין עַבְדּ֛וֹ אֽוֹ אֶת עֵ֥ין אֲמָת֖וֹ וְשִֽׁחֲתָ֑הּ לַֽחָפְשִׁ֥י יְשַׁלְּחֶ֖נּוּ תַּ֥חַת עֵינֽוֹ

verses.restored: And if he knocks out tooth of his male servant or tooth of his female servant, he shall send the servant away free for the tooth.

familiar.text: And if he smite out his manservant’s tooth, or his maidservant’s tooth; he shall let him go free for his tooth’s sake.

modern.text: And if he knocks out the tooth of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the tooth.

original.text: וְאִם שֵׁ֥ן עַבְדּ֛וֹ אֽוֹ שֵׁ֥ן אֲמָת֖וֹ יַפִּ֑יל לַֽחָפְשִׁ֥י יְשַׁלְּחֶ֖נּוּ תַּ֥חַת שִׁנּֽוֹ

verses.restored: When an ox gores a man or woman and that one dies, stoning, the ox shall be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; owner of ox is clear.

familiar.text: If an ox gore a man or a woman, that they die: then the ox shall be surely stoned, and his flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox shall be quit.

modern.text: If an ox gores a man or woman to death, the ox must surely be stoned, and its meat must not be eaten. But the owner of the ox shall not be held responsible.

original.text: וְכִֽי יִגַּ֨ח שׁ֥וֹר אֶת אִ֛ישׁ א֥וֹ אֶת אִשָּׁ֖ה וָמֵ֑ת סָק֨וֹל יִסָּקֵ֜ל הַשּׁ֗וֹר וְלֹ֤א יֵאָכֵל֙ אֶת בְּשָׂר֔וֹ וּבַ֥עַל הַשּׁ֖וֹר נָקִֽי

verses.restored: But if ox was goring previously, and its owner was warned but did not keep it in, and it killed man or woman, the ox shall be stoned and its owner also shall be put to death.

familiar.text: But if the ox were wont to push with his horn in time past, and it hath been testified to his owner, and he hath not kept him in, but that he hath killed a man or a woman; the ox shall be stoned, and his owner also shall be put to death.

modern.text: But if the ox has a habit of goring, and its owner has been warned yet does not restrain it, and it kills a man or woman, then the ox must be stoned and its owner must also be put to death.

original.text: וְאִ֡ם שׁוֹר֩ נַגָּ֨ח ה֜וּא מִתְּמֹ֣ל שִׁלְשֹׁ֗ם וְהוּעַ֤ד בִּבְעָלָיו֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְרֶ֔נּוּ וְהֵמִ֥ית אִ֖ישׁ א֣וֹ אִשָּׁ֑ה הַשּׁוֹר֙ יִסָּקֵ֔ל וְגַם בְּעָלָ֖יו יוּמָֽת

verses.restored: If ransom is laid upon him, he shall give redemption of his life/soul according to all laid upon him.

familiar.text: If there be laid on him a sum of money, then he shall give for the ransom of his life whatsoever is laid upon him.

modern.text: If payment is demanded of him instead, he may redeem his life by paying the full amount demanded of him.

original.text: אִם כֹּ֖פֶר יוּשַׁ֣ת עָלָ֑יו וְנָתַן֙ פִּדְיֹ֣ן נַפְשׁ֔וֹ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר יוּשַׁ֖ת עָלָֽיו

verses.restored: Whether it gores a son or gores a daughter, according to this judgment it shall be done to him.

familiar.text: Whether he have gored a son, or have gored a daughter, according to this judgment shall it be done unto him.

modern.text: If the ox gores a son or a daughter, it shall be done to him according to the same rule.

original.text: אוֹ בֵ֥ן יִגָּ֖ח אוֹ בַ֣ת יִגָּ֑ח כַּמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט הַזֶּ֖ה יֵעָ֥שֶׂה לּֽוֹ

verses.restored: If the ox gores a male servant or female servant, he shall give thirty shekels of silver to their master, and the ox shall be stoned.

familiar.text: If the ox shall push a manservant or a maidservant; he shall give unto their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.

modern.text: If the ox gores a manservant or maidservant, the owner must pay thirty shekels of silver to the master of that servant, and the ox must be stoned.

original.text: אִם עֶ֛בֶד יִגַּ֥ח הַשּׁ֖וֹר א֣וֹ אָמָ֑ה כֶּ֣סֶף שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שְׁקָלִ֗ים יִתֵּן֙ לַֽאדֹנָ֔יו וְהַשּׁ֖וֹר יִסָּקֵֽל

verses.restored: When a man opens a pit, or when a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or donkey falls there,

familiar.text: And if a man shall open a pit, or if a man shall dig a pit, and not cover it, and an ox or an ass fall therein;

modern.text: If a man opens or digs a pit and fails to cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,

original.text: וְכִֽי יִפְתַּ֨ח אִ֜ישׁ בּ֗וֹר א֠וֹ כִּֽי יִכְרֶ֥ה אִ֛ישׁ בֹּ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יְכַסֶּ֑נּוּ וְנָֽפַל שָׁ֥מָּה שּׁ֖וֹר א֥וֹ חֲמֽוֹר

verses.restored: owner of pit shall make restitution; silver he shall return to its owner, and dead animal shall be his.

familiar.text: The owner of the pit shall make it good, and give money unto the owner of them; and the dead beast shall be his.

modern.text: the owner of the pit shall make restitution; he must pay its owner, and the dead animal will be his.

original.text: בַּ֤עַל הַבּוֹר֙ יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם כֶּ֖סֶף יָשִׁ֣יב לִבְעָלָ֑יו וְהַמֵּ֖ת יִֽהְיֶה לּֽוֹ

verses.restored: When one man's ox strikes ox of his companion so that it dies, they shall sell live ox and divide silver, and also divide dead animal.

familiar.text: And if one man’s ox hurt another’s, that he die; then they shall sell the live ox, and divide the money of it; and the dead ox also they shall divide.

modern.text: If a man’s ox injures his neighbor’s ox and it dies, they must sell the live one and divide the proceeds; they also must divide the dead animal.

original.text: וְכִֽי יִגֹּ֧ף שֽׁוֹר אִ֛ישׁ אֶת שׁ֥וֹר רֵעֵ֖הוּ וָמֵ֑ת וּמָ֨כְר֜וּ אֶת הַשּׁ֤וֹר הַחַי֙ וְחָצ֣וּ אֶת כַּסְפּ֔וֹ וְגַ֥ם אֶת הַמֵּ֖ת יֶֽחֱצֽוּן

verses.restored: Or if it was known that the ox was goring previously, and its owner did not keep it in, repaying, he shall repay ox for ox, and dead animal shall be his.

familiar.text: Or if it be known that the ox hath used to push in time past, and his owner hath not kept him in; he shall surely pay ox for ox; and the dead shall be his own.

modern.text: But if it was known that the ox had a habit of goring, yet its owner failed to restrain it, he shall pay full compensation, ox for ox, and the dead animal will be his.

original.text: א֣וֹ נוֹדַ֗ע כִּ֠י שׁ֣וֹר נַגָּ֥ח הוּא֙ מִתְּמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמְרֶ֖נּוּ בְּעָלָ֑יו שַׁלֵּ֨ם יְשַׁלֵּ֥ם שׁוֹר֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשּׁ֔וֹר וְהַמֵּ֖ת יִֽהְיֶה לּֽוֹ

translation_notes: These are ancient covenant ordinances within a slaveholding society; preserve source wording while refusing to normalize slavery as moral ideal.
Hebrew servant release in seventh year partially limits debt-servitude, but does not erase the injustice of ownership systems.
Female servant laws contain protections against sale, deprivation, and abandonment but remain patriarchal and require ethical audit.
Human theft/kidnapping is a capital offense, directly undercutting chattel-slavery logic.
Lex talionis likely functions as proportional justice limitation rather than vengeance escalation.
Verses 20-21 are morally troubling and must be flagged; verse 26-27 grants freedom for bodily injury to servants.
safety_note: Do not use Exodus 21 to justify slavery, patriarchy, domestic violence, or corporal punishment. This is ancient legal material requiring historical-critical and ethical framing. The restored layer preserves the text; application must be governed by liberation, human dignity, anti-domination, and the broader trajectory of release from bondage.
